category_title: Emotionally disturbed primary student with trauma-related behavioral outbursts
minimal_context: Jamal is sitting at his desk in a large classroom and is asked to write the basic alphabet on his paper.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Jamal, it is time to practice our letters. Please take your pencil and write the basic alphabet on your paper.

STUDENT: (Pouts his lips) I can't see! My foot hurts...

TUTOR: You can see fine from your desk. Just start with the letter A.

STUDENT: I have to go to the bathroom! My pencil broke!

TUTOR: We need to finish writing the alphabet first, then you can go.

STUDENT: (Starts crying and kicks at his desk) I can't do it! (Tears his paper)

options.A: Provide a clear beginning and end for each basic alphabet writing task, ensuring Jamal understands exactly when the activity starts and finishes during the classroom session.
options.B: Increase the time allotted for the alphabet writing lessons, extending the duration of the activity from fifteen minutes to thirty minutes during the large classroom sessions.
options.C: Have Jamal practice writing the basic alphabet on an iPad by tracing along the screen with his finger instead of using his pencil and paper at his desk.
options.D: Implement a color-coded behavior chart to track Jamal's behavior across seven levels, proceeding from the lowest level of needing parent contact to the highest level of super principled.
